s1.syndrome_frame: Painless testicular swelling with associated adrenal gland abnormalities
salient_findings: Enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
key_facts: 82-year-old man
Painless right testicular swelling of several weeks’ duration
No systemic symptoms
History of glaucoma, prostatic adenomectomy, and hernioplasty
Medications: dorzolamide, lansoprazole, and dutasteride
Testicular ultrasound showed enlargement and inhomogeneity of the right testis and epididymis
Ipsilateral hydrocele
No response to 10 days of amoxicillin–clavulanate
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT confirmed testicular pathology and revealed new bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement
Adrenal nodules were absent on a CT scan 3 years earlier
18 FDG PET/CT showed intense uptake in the right testis but no uptake in the adrenal glands
Normal laboratory evaluation results
No asthenia, headaches, abdominal pain, striae, or “buffalo hump”

shortlist.label: Leydig cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Painless testicular swelling and intense uptake on FDG PET/CT

shortlist.label: testicular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular swelling and lack of response to antibiotics

shortlist.label: adrenal myelolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral macronodular adrenal enlargement with no uptake on FDG PET/CT

shortlist.label: testicular sex cord-stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Testicular swelling and association with adrenal gland abnormalities

shortlist.label: adrenal rest tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Association with testicular pathology and adrenal gland enlargement

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with painless testicular swelling and the ultrasound findings of testicular enlargement and inhomogeneity, along with the intense uptake on the 18 FDG PET/CT, are consistent with a testicular tumor. The lack of systemic symptoms and normal laboratory evaluation results also support this diagnosis. Leydig cell tumor is a type of sex cord-stromal tumor that can present with testicular swelling and is consistent with the patient's age and clinical presentation.

rejected.label: testicular lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphoma would likely show systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory results, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: adrenal myelolipoma
rejected.why: The adrenal nodules showed no uptake on the 18 FDG PET/CT, and myelolipoma would not explain the testicular findings.

rejected.label: testicular sex cord-stromal tumor
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes Leydig cell tumor, but Leydig cell tumor is a more specific diagnosis that fits the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: adrenal rest tumor
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with a primary testicular tumor rather than an adrenal rest tumor.
